text:
WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: Send the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act to President Trump’s Desk

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

"Last night, landmark permitting reform legislation passed the Senate. It's one of the biggest things that you will see. It's a big deal… It’s projected to put at least $1,300 a year back in the pockets of hardworking Americans.” – President Donald J. Trump

President Donald J. Trump is committed to fixing America’s broken permitting system standing behind (BAAJA), legislation that will modernize federal environmental reviews and permitting while delivering cheaper energy, high-paying jobs, and economic growth across the United States.

Last night, the Senate advanced landmark permitting reform legislation, and now the House has the opportunity to finish the job and send the bill to President Trump’s desk to lock in generations of affordability and energy dominance for the American people.

Here’s what they’re saying about the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act:

American Exploration & Production Council CEO Anne Bradbury: “AXPC applauds the Senate for taking decisive bipartisan action to remove longstanding barriers to American energy and infrastructure development. BAAJA offers a generational opportunity to cut through permitting delays and lower costs across America without compromising critical environmental protections. With meaningful relief for American families within reach, we respectfully urge the House to send BAAJA to the President’s desk before the end of the year.”

American Chemistry Council: “Yesterday’s vote represents an important step toward addressing longstanding permitting challenges that have delayed projects, increased costs, and hindered economic growth. As demand for energy, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure continues to grow, the United States needs a permitting system capable of supporting investment and development at the speed required to compete globally.

“The future of American manufacturing, infrastructure, and energy development depends on our nation's ability to build. Enactment of this legislation would help ensure the United States remains the best place in the world to invest, manufacture, and innovate “

American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers: “Today’s bipartisan Senate vote marks a major breakthrough on historic permitting reforms that would deliver more affordable energy for consumers, cut costly delays, and build much-needed critical infrastructure. We thank Senators Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich for advancing long-overdue reforms.”

Association of American Railroads CEO and President Ian Jefferies: “Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an encouraging step toward a permitting process that works better for communities and the projects they depend on. Freight railroads make long-term investments in the network that connects businesses, farms, ports, and consumers. When reviews take years, needed improvements can be delayed. This bipartisan legislation can help make project reviews timelier and more predictable while preserving important environmental protections.”

Business Roundtable CEO Joshua Bolten: “Business Roundtable applauds the Senate for passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. The strong bipartisan vote marks an important step toward enacting comprehensive permitting reforms that would help lower costs for American families and businesses.

“By modernizing the federal permitting system, this legislation would make it easier to build critical energy projects, roads, ports and other much-needed infrastructure. The benefits would flow to Americans in the form of lower utility bills, new good-paying jobs and more private-sector investment in communities across the country. We urge the House to finish the job and swiftly pass this measure.”

Interstate Natural Gas Association of America President and CEO Amy Andryszak: “Tonight’s Senate vote marks a pivotal step toward modernizing America’s permitting process and ensuring affordable energy for American consumers. Enshrining improvements to the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), judicial reviews, and permit certainty in statute will help accelerate the buildout of the critical energy infrastructure needed to meet growing demand and ensure a reliable, affordable energy future.

“We applaud Senators for reaching bipartisan consensus and urge the U.S. House of Representatives to act quickly to send this legislation to the President’s desk. The House must pass this legislation without further delay to help meet America’s energy needs and address rising energy costs.”

Laborers International Union of North America President Brent Booker: “For more than a decade, endless permitting delays have stalled critical infrastructure projects that put our members to work across the country. Every month a project sits on the shelf, LIUNA members go without paychecks. This bill ends the runaround. It sets clear timelines and holds the process accountable, so projects get decided and built. Congress has spent years talking about the need to fix our broken permitting process. Now it has a real opportunity to do something about it. The cost of inaction is too high: lost jobs, lost investment, and lost opportunities for working Americans. We cannot afford to let another Congress come and go while critical projects remain stalled and working families pay the price.”

National Association of Home Builders: “With so many families priced out of the market, the House must pass this bill without delay. BAAJA will make federal permits faster and less costly for builders and developers, lowering land development costs and making lots more affordable. It also helps multifamily developers by ensuring that the use of federal grants and loans does not automatically trigger a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review. For projects that still need a NEPA review, the bill sets enforceable deadlines for agencies to complete it.”

National Electrical Manufacturers Association President and CEO Debra Phillips: “America’s electricity needs are growing rapidly, and this legislation will help us build the infrastructure to meet them. It speeds up transmission projects, encourages grid-enhancing advanced transmission technologies, and gives investors more certainty, which means more reliable, affordable power for consumers. That will help America build the energy system our future demands, and move past an outdated permitting system that has been tangled in red tape for too long. We commend the bipartisan leadership that made this progress possible and urge the House to finish the job.”

National Mining Association President and CEO Rich Nolan: “We’re grateful to the Senate for coming together to move legislation that will help transform American potential into American production, and for the leadership of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich, who deserve great credit for their tireless work to advance the bill. True economic and national security comes with a United States that can build things again, using domestic materials and domestic fuels, and decisively confront China’s supply chain dominance. It’s now up to the House to say American prosperity and competitiveness matter, ensure that made in America can also be mined in America, and pass this legislation.”

National Rural Electric Cooperative Association CEO Jim Matheson: “This legislation will dramatically improve the federal permitting system, making it more manageable and predictable for electric co-ops as they work to keep the lights on at a cost families and businesses can afford. Today’s environmental review processes can take years, delaying critical energy projects and increasing costs that ultimately fall on consumers. The bill will streamline reviews and reduce litigation delays, while leaving important environmental protections in place.”

U.S. Oil and Gas Association President Tim Stewart: "BAAJA brought together the broadest and most diverse coalition of working interests that Washington has seen in decades who worked to pass a good piece of legislation that will let us build things in America again.

“It will ensure greater abundance and affordability for the next generation and we are proud to be a part of it.”

Western Energy Alliance: “We have a generational choice in front of us. We must decide if we’re going to be builders or not. If we’re going to meet our nation’s energy needs, or not. Reforming the nation’s outdated permitting system is critical to delivering affordable energy and growing jobs. Our nation’s economy can no longer sustain the strategy of activist groups to defer, delay, and deny high-value energy and infrastructure projects. This bill is an important step toward providing greater certainty, while still prioritizing the environment. It broadly benefits infrastructure development and all sources of energy production. We’re pleased to see senators come together in bipartisan manner to work out key differences for the benefit of the American people. We now urge lawmakers in the House to take the deal and deliver a win on energy affordability before the current session
ends.”

Distributed on November 20th, 2026.

text:
Alabama Power is offering a rate reduction of about $160 million for 2027, starting with January bills.
Savings for residential customers
Savings depend on electricity use (compared with current rates at the same usage):
•  1,000 kWh/month (a common benchmark): more than $50 per year
•  750 kWh/month: about $40 per year
•  2,000 kWh/month: about $106 per year
The lower rate applies automatically to every monthly bill—no action is required from customers. Actual bills will still vary with usage and weather.
Why the decrease
The reduction is driven mainly by expected higher revenue in 2027 from large-load data centers. Alabama Power says these customers pay the full cost to serve them, which lowers the cost to serve other customers.
This announcement was made today (November 20, 2026) via a filing with the Alabama Public Service Commission. It follows an earlier commitment to freeze rates through 2027.

text:
Nick Saban says a former Alabama player who played pre-NIL told him getting paid $2,000,000 in college might have prevented him from becoming the man he became

“Who are you going to pay? What positions are most important? Because if you pay the wrong guys, and you’ve heard me say this before, you’re out of luck. When you can’t evaluate the players and you don’t pay the right guys, you’re going to pay the consequences for that in the future.”

“You’re going to spend all this money, you’re not going to have a very good team, and you’re not going to get the outcome everybody expects. And then the cause and effect of paying players is we’re raising money from alumni who now think they should have a say in what happens. And that’s why 33 coaches got fired last year, because of boosters. They have a say.”

“Look, talent is not talent if you can’t use it. So if you don’t have character to go with it, you probably can’t use it. And it’s not just in sports. Nobody who’s not really smart gets into medical school, but everybody doesn’t make it.”

“They’re talented enough, but they don’t make it. Some of them who make it don’t make very good doctors. So I always say talent is not talent if you can’t use it, which means you have to have some kind of competitive character to make the choices and decisions to create the habits. So you can recruit talent, but accountability and commitment you have to develop.”

“And most of the time you can develop it. So it’s going to be the coaches who can judge character, but then also have the ability to help their players create those things. Don’t let the money change you. Stay focused on the things you can control to develop value for your future, because there’s a lot more value out there.”

“But I will say one thing that’s very interesting to me. Former players who played for us, I’m not mentioning any names. They didn’t make the money, they didn’t get paid. They played, they created value, they made a lot of money in the NFL, and they played for a long time.”

“And one of them said to me the other day something that was kind of alarming. He said, ‘If I would have gotten paid $2 million when I played here, I don’t know if I would have become the man I became. I don’t know if I would have developed into the player I became. I don’t know that I wouldn’t have, but I don’t know if I could have handled that at 18 and 19 years old, and I don’t know if I would have become what I was able to become.’”

text:
Axe Compute Q3 2026 Earnings: Revenue More Than Doubles

Axe Compute’s Q3 2026 results show how quickly the institutional demand for AI infrastructure is taking shape, and why its relationship with Aethir matters.

Revenue reached $7.2M, up 125% from $3.2M in Q2. 
All revenue came from GPU compute services, a clear signal that demand is moving beyond infrastructure promises into actual service delivery.

Net income came in at $11.5M, compared with a $17.2M loss in Q2. However, this figure included $10.5M in digital asset gains and a $4.6M non-cash unrealized gain. So, it’s important not to confuse reported net income with operating profitability.

The bigger story is the contract pipeline.

By September 29, Axe had signed contracts worth more than $3.45B, including over $2.8B from three July Build contracts across the US and Europe, plus a Georgia agreement worth more than $350M over five years.

These are contract values, not revenue already earned. Execution is now the real test.

In Georgia, Axe acquired a 2,304-unit NVIDIA B300 GPU cluster, comprising 288 Supermicro B300 NVL8 servers, with approximately 5MW of committed power. The $124.4M acquisition was provisioned by quarter-end, with customer acceptance still underway and commissioning expected between Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.

Another important metric: contract liabilities climbed to $569.3M, largely reflecting customer prepayments and deferred revenue. These prepayments help fund infrastructure deployment, although they also come with the responsibility to deliver the contracted compute.

This is where the Aethir connection becomes interesting.

@AethirCloud brings distributed GPU infrastructure and global compute capacity, while Axe provides an enterprise-facing commercial structure for large customers and contracts. Through initiatives like ACCELERATE, the relationship aims to expand institutional-grade GPU infrastructure across the US and Europe.

The takeaway? AI infrastructure is becoming a serious commercial market, and the competition is shifting from simply securing GPUs to delivering reliable compute at scale.

Axe CEO’s message captures the next phase perfectly: “Our job now is delivery.”

2026 has brought the contracts and the numbers. 2027 will show how much of that opportunity can become operational capacity and recognized revenue.
